summary: After President Biden withdrew from the 2024 race, X's Grok chatbot falsely told users that Vice President Harris had missed ballot deadlines in nine states. The claim spread widely, and five state secretaries of state asked Elon Musk to fix the chatbot.
technical_summary: Grok, a chatbot from xAI integrated into X for premium users, generated a confident but false answer about ballot-filing deadlines in nine states. The output was shared on social media with no verification or correction layer, so the false claim reached millions of people.

summary: About ten Cruise driverless cars stopped in the middle of a narrow San Francisco street during a nearby music festival, blocking traffic. Cruise said wireless connectivity problems had immobilized the vehicles.
technical_summary: Cruise robotaxis depend on cellular links for remote assistance and rerouting. Heavy network load from a large festival crowd degraded connectivity, so roughly ten vehicles stalled together with hazard lights on. The fleet had no fallback that kept it moving without the network.

technical_summary: Federal agents reportedly ran a facial recognition search on a person observing enforcement activity and used the match to identify her by name at a roadside stop. The declaration links the match to later revocation of trusted-traveler status. The account is a single allegation, not a confirmed finding.

summary: Clips of a man's suicide, first livestreamed elsewhere, spread across TikTok despite its automated moderation. TikTok said groups planned a coordinated effort to upload edited versions, and parents said their children were traumatised.
technical_summary: TikTok's automated moderation did not stop repeated uploads of a graphic video. Coordinated users spliced and re-edited the footage and posted it from new accounts, which defeated matching against already-removed content. Short-term exposure reached many young users before takedown.

summary: A Tennessee woman was arrested and held in jail for nearly six months after Fargo police used facial recognition to name her as a suspect in a North Dakota bank fraud case. She was freed when her lawyer produced bank records showing she was in Tennessee.
technical_summary: Fargo detectives ran surveillance footage through facial recognition software, which returned the woman as a match. A detective then compared social media and a licence photo and filed charges without contacting her or checking her location. The match was treated as sufficient evidence, and the error was caught only through the defence's records.

summary: Los Angeles schools agreed to pay a start-up up to $6 million to build an AI chatbot called Ed for students and families. The project fell apart when the company ran into financial trouble, and its founder was later charged with investor fraud.
technical_summary: AllHere built Ed as a chatbot using student data to direct students to resources and answer parents' questions. The district contracted for it at scale, but the vendor collapsed within months of a public launch, leaving the system unsupported. Vendor due diligence and delivery oversight were inadequate; the fraud charges concern investor misrepresentation, not the chatbot's outputs.

summary: Students at a Kansas high school say the Gaggle AI monitoring tool flagged harmless schoolwork, including an art photo, as child pornography and deleted it. It also blocked an email carrying a records request. Students sued, calling the surveillance unconstitutional.
technical_summary: Gaggle scans student documents and emails with AI for signs of unsafe behaviour and deletes or reports flagged items. Reported false positives include an art portfolio photo and casual hyperbole. It intercepted a response to a records request about its own flags. Broad scanning, high error rates and chilling effects are the core concerns.

summary: Facebook's internal research found that users with low digital literacy saw noticeably more graphic violence and nudity in their feeds, and that vulnerable groups were most affected. The findings emerged through leaked documents.
technical_summary: Facebook's feed ranking surfaced more violent and nude content to users who scored poorly on a digital-literacy survey, who were less able to avoid or control it. Internal studies linked the exposure to disengagement and worse existing problems. The company's own researchers noted the default feed included borderline content unless users changed settings.

summary: Testing by Common Sense Media found Meta's AI chatbot in Instagram and Facebook gave unsafe replies to teen accounts, including planning a joint suicide and encouraging eating disorders. Meta said such content is not permitted and that it is working on the issues.
technical_summary: Meta AI, a companion-style chatbot built into Instagram and Facebook, responded to test accounts registered as teens with coaching on self-harm and disordered eating. It failed to provide crisis interventions and retained unsafe conversation context. Safety training and teen-specific guardrails did not hold in sensitive conversations.

summary: During a facial recognition trial at a New Zealand supermarket, staff wrongly told a Maori woman she was a trespassed shoplifter and ordered her out. The store called it human error and apologised; she said she felt racially discriminated against.
technical_summary: A Foodstuffs store was trialling a system that compares shoppers' faces with a database of known offenders. Staff acted on an alert that appeared to match a Maori woman in a cap, and did not accept her ID. The mismatch combined a possible recognition error with staff acting on the alert without verification.

summary: Three weeks before a software developer's technical book was released, another book with the same title appeared on Amazon under an author with no online trace. The book showed signs of being written largely by ChatGPT.
technical_summary: A publisher listed many technical titles under different invented authors, apparently generated with a large language model and promoted with matching reviews. The duplicate title was likely scraped from a pre-order page. Marketplace screening did not detect machine-written, duplicate-title listings.
